sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普林。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，每晚你都要带着300张最珍爱的唱片去上班，然后把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成这样一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，摆满了美丽的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, in 2012, a woman raised her hand and asked if the city of Charlottesville, Virginia should remove a statue of General Robert E.
sentences.zh: 今天，在2012年，一位女性举手提问，询问弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔市是否应该移除市中心公园里的一座罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee from a downtown park.
sentences.zh: 李将军的雕像。

sentences.en: The chain of events that led from that question to Saturday's violence.
sentences.zh: 正是这一问题引发了一系列连锁事件，最终导致了周六的暴力冲突。

sentences.en: And racism is evil, the president says, two days after the violence erupted in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 总统在夏洛茨维尔暴力事件爆发两天后表示，种族主义是邪恶的。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, August 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月15日，星期二。

sentences.en: My name is Kristen Sakas.
sentences.zh: 我叫克里斯滕·萨卡斯。

sentences.en: I've been on the Charlottesville City Council for eight years.
sentences.zh: 我在夏洛茨维尔市议会工作了八年。

sentences.en: I have lived in Charlottesville for 22 years and love my city.
sentences.zh: 我在夏洛茨维尔生活了22年，我热爱我的城市。

sentences.en: When I moved here, our family noticed these two large Confederate statues in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 当我搬到这里时，我们家人注意到夏洛茨维尔有两座大型的邦联雕像。

sentences.en: But Robert E.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯特·E·

sentences.en: Lee is by far the most dominant.
sentences.zh: 李的雕像无疑是最显眼的。

sentences.en: It's in a central park of our city, overlooking the downtown, kind of in a high pride of place.
sentences.zh: 它位于我们城市的中央公园，俯瞰着市中心，可以说是占据了一个备受推崇的重要位置。

sentences.en: And it was startling, because we had heard that Charlottesville was this wonderfully welcoming place.
sentences.zh: 这让人感到震惊，因为我们听说夏洛茨维尔是一个无比热情好客的地方。

sentences.en: We have an interracial family.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个跨种族家庭。

sentences.en: And when we saw those statues, we wondered, you know, why is Charlottesville glorifying heroes of the Confederacy if it really is a place that's interested in racial equity?
sentences.zh: 当我们看到这些雕像时，我们不禁想，如果夏洛茨维尔真的致力于实现种族平等，为什么还要美化邦联英雄呢？

sentences.en: And so in 2012, when I was on city council, I went to a lecture of an historian.
sentences.zh: 所以在2012年，当时我是市议员，我去听了一位历史学家的讲座。

sentences.en: In our time thinking about the South here, based in Virginia, one of the more monumentalized places in America, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 在我们回溯这里南方的历史时——这里位于弗吉尼亚州，可以说是美国纪念碑最多的地方之一。

sentences.en: Talking about the kind of practice of putting up these monuments to the Confederacy in the early 1920s.
sentences.zh: 谈到在20世纪20年代初竖立这些邦联纪念碑的做法。

sentences.en: We've seen lots of different kinds of monuments to the past of all the humans that have enacted things here before us.
sentences.zh: 我们见证了各种各样关于过去的纪念碑，为了纪念所有曾在我们之前在这里创造历史的人类。

sentences.en: And our challenge has been to figure out what these are monuments to,
sentences.zh: 我们的挑战不仅在于弄清楚这些到底是什么纪念碑，

sentences.en: but also what they say about the people who built them, and also about what our response to them says about us.
sentences.zh: 还要弄清楚它们对建造者意味着什么，以及我们对它们的反应说明了我们是怎样的人。

sentences.en: And that they were really part of the resurgence of this sort of myth of Southern white greatness when white people were in charge in the South and everything was wonderful
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是南方白人掌权、一切都美好的时代里，南方白人伟大神话复兴的一部分，

sentences.en: and there was honor and that is what these statues signified.
sentences.zh: 并且充满了荣耀，这就是这些雕像所象征的意义。

sentences.en: And so at the end of his lecture, you know, there was a couple of questions and then a pause.
sentences.zh: 所以在讲座结束时，你知道的，有几个提问，然后是一段沉默。

sentences.en: And so I asked the question, is it time for us to look at these monuments that are around the South and say, are these really expressing the sentiments of our people?
sentences.zh: 于是我提出了一个问题：我们是不是该审视一下南方各地的这些纪念碑，想想它们是否真的表达了我们人民的心声？

sentences.en: Is this really the kind of monuments we should be having in our cities?
sentences.zh: 这真的是我们城市里应该有的纪念碑吗？

sentences.en: And there was this gasp in the room.
sentences.zh: 房间里顿时一片倒吸凉气的声音。

sentences.en: It was, you know, like, how could you bring up such a thing?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家的反应就像是在说，你怎么能提出这种事？

sentences.en: It was a little startling to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到有点吃惊。

sentences.en: You know, I grew up in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 要知道，我在密西西比州长大。

sentences.en: My parents were both civil rights workers and you talk about these things.
sentences.zh: 我的父母都是民权工作者，你们会讨论这些事情。

sentences.en: You know, what does history mean and how do we live out that history today?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，历史意味着什么，我们今天又该如何活出这段历史？

sentences.en: As I left the lecture, a reporter who had been in the location came running up to me and asked me, do you stand by what you said in there?
sentences.zh: 当我离开讲座时，现场的一位记者跑过来问我：你支持你在里面说的话吗？

sentences.en: And I realized just even by bringing up the question, it was loaded with all sorts of angst and meaning.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，仅仅是提出这个问题，就充满了各种焦虑和含义。

sentences.en: And I said, of course, I meant it.
sentences.zh: 我说，当然，我是认真的。

sentences.en: I think we should have this conversation.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该展开这场对话。

sentences.en: And the headline the next day in the paper was, counselor suggests removing Lee statue.
sentences.zh: 第二天报纸的头条是：议员建议移除李将军雕像。

sentences.en: And I started getting phone calls and death threats.
sentences.zh: 我开始接到电话和死亡威胁。

sentences.en: Some folks, I don't know who, but in the night came and plastered
sentences.zh: 有些人，我不知道是谁，在夜里跑来把

sentences.en: Confederate stickers on the backs of our car and the driveway.
sentences.zh: 邦联贴纸贴在我们家车道上汽车的后备箱上。

sentences.en: So what happens after that?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: How does this move from a question that you posed in a informal setting, you know, with a professor of history, how does that move to an ordinance
sentences.zh: 这怎么会从你在一个非正式场合向一位历史学教授提出的一个问题，演变成市议会审议的一项

sentences.en: being taken up by the city council?
sentences.zh: 行政法令呢？

sentences.en: Over the intervening years, a lot of members of the public started contacting city council and really talking about why this was important.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几年里，许多公众开始联系市议会，认真讨论为什么这件事如此重要。

sentences.en: In all our discussions about this issue, I am convinced that this council is unanimous in feeling that these statues of fallen rebel commanders
sentences.zh: 在我们关于这个议题的所有讨论中，我深信市议会一致认为，这些阵亡叛军指挥官的雕像

sentences.en: do not represent our interpretation of history or the way we should treat our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 并不代表我们对历史的诠释，也不代表我们对待邻居应有的方式。

sentences.en: Charlottesville is one of the best cities in the country for a variety of reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于各种原因，夏洛茨维尔是全国最好的城市之一。

sentences.en: I have heard some African-American citizens of Charlottesville who feel that by continuing to glorify these Confederate monuments, especially the monument to Robert E.
sentences.zh: 我听过一些夏洛茨维尔的非裔市民说，继续美化这些邦联纪念碑——尤其是罗伯特·E·李将军的纪念碑，

sentences.en: Lee, who led the army of the Confederacy in a war to preserve the institution of slavery, that that is on its face every single day,
sentences.zh: 他曾领导邦联军队进行了一场旨在维护奴隶制体制的战争——这无异于天天都在

sentences.en: a slap in the face to people in our own community whose ancestors would have been enslaved if that fight had won.
sentences.zh: 对我们社区中那些如果当年那场战争获胜就会沦为奴隶的先辈们的后代扇耳光。

sentences.en: I have heard from white Charlottesville residents who say that the presence of those statues, especially the Robert E.
sentences.zh: 我听过夏洛茨维尔的白人居民说，这些雕像的存在，尤其是公园里的罗伯特·E·李将军雕像，

sentences.en: Lee statue in that park, conveys the idea that this city supports the ideas of the Confederacy and makes it look like they believe that, and they don't.
sentences.zh: 传达了这座城市支持邦联思想的信号，让人觉得他们赞同这些思想，然而事实并非如此。

sentences.en: I've heard from other people who say, you know, my great-great-grandfather fought for the Confederacy, and if you take that statue down, it disrespects his memory.
sentences.zh: 我也听其他人说，你知道的，我的曾曾祖父为邦联战斗过，如果你把雕像拆了，就是对他的记忆的不尊重。

sentences.en: My name is Jason Kessler.
sentences.zh: 我叫杰森·凯斯勒。

sentences.en: I've lived in the city of Charlottesville for over 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我在夏洛茨维尔市住了十多年。

sentences.en: I was born here.
sentences.zh: 我出生在这里。

sentences.en: My family are from here.
sentences.zh: 我的家人来自这里。

sentences.en: My ancestors are Confederate veterans.
sentences.zh: 我的祖先是邦联老兵。

sentences.en: I believe in the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 我信仰第一修正案。

sentences.en: I believe in the right for people to peaceably assemble and speak their minds.
sentences.zh: 我相信人们有和平集会和表达意见的权利。

sentences.en: Some of the meetings we had, people who brought Confederate flags and guns.
sentences.zh: 在我们举行的一些会议上，有人带了邦联旗帜和枪支。

sentences.en: As I was saying, every day you guys come up here and talk about black people, you talk about gay people, you don't give a damn about white people.
sentences.zh: 就像我刚才说的，你们每天来到这里讨论黑人，讨论同性恋，却根本不在乎白人。

sentences.en: And white people have a right to organize and advocate for our rights as well.
sentences.zh: 白人同样有权利组织起来，为我们的权益大声疾呼。

sentences.en: You people are implementing policies which are displacing us in our home countries.
sentences.zh: 你们这些人正在推行一些政策，让我们在自己的祖国被边缘化。

sentences.en: Second.
sentences.zh: 第二点。

sentences.en: For those of you enjoying the dark recesses of the Internet, we are not voting to destroy the statue or to bury it.
sentences.zh: 对于那些喜欢泡在互联网阴暗角落里的人，我们不是在投票摧毁这座雕像，也不是要把它埋了。

sentences.en: So stop with the ISIS comparisons.
sentences.zh: 所以别再拿它跟IS作比较了。

sentences.en: They make you look foolish and taint the important argument of those who say, leave it where it is because it has historical and educational value.
sentences.zh: 这显得你们很愚蠢，也玷污了那些主张“因为它具有历史和教育价值而将其留在原地”的人所提出的重要论点。

sentences.en: And then earlier this year, we took a vote of whether to move the Robert E.
sentences.zh: 然后就在今年早些时候，我们对是否迁移罗伯特·E·李将军雕像进行了投票，结果是三票赞成迁移，两票反对。

sentences.en: Lee statue and we had three votes to move it and two not.
sentences.zh: 今晚的头条新闻：

sentences.en: First tonight,
sentences.zh: 夏洛茨维尔市议会投票决定将邦联将军罗伯特·E·李的雕像从市中心移走。

sentences.en: Charlottesville City Council voted to move the statue of Confederate General Robert E.
sentences.zh: 是的，最终投票结果是三比二，鲍勃·芬威克在上次投票弃权导致平局后，这次投了赞成票。

sentences.en: Lee out of downtown.
sentences.zh: 因此，特此决议，夏洛茨维尔市应将罗伯特·E·李将军的雕像

sentences.en: Yeah, the final vote was three to two with Bob Fenwick voting for the move after abstaining last vote, leaving it in a tie.
sentences.zh: 从目前被称为李公园的公园中移除；并特此决议，目前被称为李公园的公园应被重新命名；并特此决议，

sentences.en: Now, therefore, be it resolved that the City of Charlottesville shall remove the statue of Robert E.
sentences.zh: 我们特此指示工作人员在60天内向市议会提交一系列推荐方案，供我们审议，

sentences.en: Lee from the park currently known as Lee Park and be it further resolved that the park currently known as Lee Park shall be renamed and be it further resolved
sentences.zh: 以便就雕像目的地、设计和公园名称做出最终决定。

sentences.en: that we hereby direct staff to bring Council a range of recommended options for moving forward with decisions on destination, design, and park name within 60 days
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: for our consideration.
sentences.zh: 向你们的体制顶礼膜拜吧，诸位。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bow to your system, everyone.
sentences.zh: 还有人要补充吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在我们要继续了。

sentences.en: Any further?
sentences.zh: 我们要进入...

sentences.en: Okay, now we're going to move on.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，在过去的两天里，我通过电子邮件和当面交流听取了许多人的意见，他们说：

sentences.en: We're going to move on to...
sentences.zh: 我过去认为这些雕像应该留下来。

sentences.en: I will say that in the past two days, I have heard from a lot of people, both through email and in person, people who said, you know,
sentences.zh: 我过去认为这无关紧要，它只是一尊雕像。

sentences.en: I used to think that those statues should stay.
sentences.zh: 但这个周末这些白人至上主义者利用这些雕像来宣称“这就是我所代表的立场”，这让我明白了为什么必须把它们移走。

sentences.en: I used to think that it didn't matter and that it was just a statue.
sentences.zh: 真有意思，那竟然成了这场辩论的催化剂。

sentences.en: And the presence of these white supremacists this weekend using those statues to say that's what I stand for has made me understand why they need to be taken away.
sentences.zh: 那么，议员女士，这个周末你在现场吗？

sentences.en: That's really interesting that that was an accelerant in the debate.
sentences.zh: 是的，虽然我没有卷入大部分的冲突中心。

sentences.en: So, Councilwoman, were you there this weekend?
sentences.zh: 我大概在冲突的外围。

sentences.en: Yes, although I was not in the middle of most of the fray.
sentences.zh: 我觉得以我的身份出现在那里，可能只会激化矛盾，无济于事。

sentences.en: I was kind of on the outskirts of it.
sentences.zh: 所以我有个问题想问你，因为我们谈到这时我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: I felt that being there might, as who I am, probably would only inflame tempers and wouldn't help.
sentences.zh: 你当时坐在那个房间里向一位教授提出那个问题，可以说，夏洛茨维尔这整场事件链就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: So, I want to ask you a question because I've been thinking about this as we're talking.
sentences.zh: 然后你又经历了本周末的事件，这对你来说相当痛苦。

sentences.en: You're in that room asking a professor that question and you can argue that that's how this entire chain of events here starts in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是如何看待这一切的，以及你在其中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: And then you have the events of this weekend, which are quite painful for you.
sentences.zh: 并不是说要暗示你负有个人责任，而是你如何消化这一切。

sentences.en: And I wonder how you process that, your own role in all this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，实际上有很多电子邮件都在说：“这全都是你的错。”

sentences.en: Not to suggest personal responsibility, but how you process that.
sentences.zh: “如果你当时没提那事，根本就不会有人这么做。”

sentences.en: You know, there actually have been a lot of emails saying, you know, it's all your fault.
sentences.zh: 但我就是不这么认为。

sentences.en: If you hadn't brought that up, nobody would be doing this.
sentences.zh: 我认为，即使当时这里没发生，也可能会在其他地方发生。

sentences.en: And I just don't believe it.
sentences.zh: 但不能因为有人最终会对你做正确的事做出恶劣反应，就成为你不去做正确之事的理由。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, if it hadn't been here, it might have been somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些雕像问题，其实是我们国家长期以来关于种族、历史和正义等从未真正完成的对话的一个替代话题。

sentences.en: But the fact that somebody might eventually react badly to you doing the right thing is not a reason to not do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得当人们谈论雕像时，他们并不是真的在谈论雕像本身。

sentences.en: You know, these issues, the statues are kind of a proxy for a conversation that we've never really completed in this country around race and around history, around justice.
sentences.zh: 他们是在谈论自己在美国社会中扮演什么角色。

sentences.en: And so I think when people talk about the statues, they're not really talking about statues.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在本周末的游行中看到，这个国家有一些白人真的相信他们处于危险之中，

sentences.en: They're talking about where they see their own role in America.
sentences.zh: 相信他们最终会因为种族多样性和包容性而被消灭。

sentences.en: I think we saw in this demonstration this weekend that there are white people in this country who really believe that they are in danger, that somehow they're going
sentences.zh: 虽然我可以对此付诸一笑，说这显然不是真的，但我认为，其中表达出的一些情绪，

sentences.en: to be eliminated because of racial diversity and inclusion.
sentences.zh: 已经远超了一尊雕像是否应该留在弗吉尼亚州某个小镇的特定公园里的范畴。

sentences.en: And while I could laugh about that and say, you know, that's clearly not true, I think that something in there is being expressed that's way beyond whether a statue stays or not
sentences.zh: 他受重伤了！

sentences.en: in a particular park in a particular town in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他受重伤了！

sentences.en: It's badly hurt.
sentences.zh: 我们现在需要急救人员！

sentences.en: It's badly hurt.
sentences.zh: 操！

sentences.en: We need paramedics right now.
sentences.zh: 那辆车直接撞进人群里了！

sentences.en: Holy shit.
sentences.zh: 议员女士，此时此刻你还有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: The car just drove into people.
sentences.zh: 因为如你所知，所有人的目光都聚焦在你们的城市上。

sentences.en: Councilwoman, is there anything else you want to say in this moment?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想说的是，作为密西西比州民权工作者的孩子，

sentences.en: Because as you know well, all eyes are on your city.
sentences.zh: 如果我们以为在关于雕像的讨论出现之前一切都好，那就大错特错了。

sentences.en: Well, I will say that as the child of civil rights workers in Mississippi,
